title: Substantial performance and minor defects
summary: Substantial performance can permit recovery of the contract price, with an adjustment for defects, where the party has performed the essential undertaking and the remaining departure does not justify treating the exchange as failed.
notes:
Jacob & Youngs involved pipe from manufacturers other than the specified brand, discovered after a house was complete. The quality and function of the installed pipe, the character of the omission, the purpose of the specification, and the destructive cost of replacement mattered. The decision distinguished the right to payment from the measure of damages for the defect.

Substantial performance does not make every deviation harmless or erase express risk allocations. A deliberate or material departure can lead to a different result. Plante, Groves, and Peevyhouse later ask related but distinct questions about the cost of completion and loss in value. The materiality of breach, the payment condition, and the damages measure should each be addressed.
